runtime_row.subject: Maths
runtime_row.subtopic: Basic Proportionality Theorem — Statement, Proof, and Application
runtime_row.questionText:
(a) State and prove Basic Proportionality theorem.
(b) In the given figure ∠CEF = ∠CFE. F is the midpoint of DC. Prove that AB/BD = AE/FD.
runtime_row.answer: (a) BPT proved with statement, given/to-prove, figure, and reasoned proof. (b) AB/BD = AE/FD proved using BPT in Δ ABE and midpoint theorem in Δ CDG.
solutionSteps: Part (a) — Statement of BPT: If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle, intersecting the other two sides at distinct points, it divides those two sides in the same ratio.

Part (a) — Given Δ ABC with DE ‖ BC, D on AB, E on AC. To prove: AD/DB = AE/EC. Construction: join BE and CD; draw EM ⊥ AB and DN ⊥ AC. Proof: Area(ΔADE) = (1/2)·AD·EM and Area(ΔBDE) = (1/2)·DB·EM, so Area(ΔADE)/Area(ΔBDE) = AD/DB. Similarly Area(ΔADE)/Area(ΔDEC) = AE/EC. Triangles BDE and DEC have equal areas (same base DE, same parallel line BC). Therefore AD/DB = AE/EC.
Part (b) — Construction: draw DG ‖ BE meeting CA produced at G. In Δ ABE, since DG ‖ BE, by BPT: AB/BD = AE/GE  ... (i)

Part (b) — In Δ CDG, F is midpoint of DC and FE ‖ DG (because DG ‖ BE ‖ FE not needed; instead use that GE/CE = DF/CF). By midpoint theorem applied to Δ CDG with F midpoint of CD, E is midpoint of CG, so CE = GE  ... (ii)

Part (b) — Given ∠CEF = ∠CFE in Δ CFE ⇒ CF = CE (sides opposite equal angles) ... (iii). F is midpoint of DC ⇒ CF = FD ... (iv). Combining (ii), (iii), (iv): GE = CE = CF = FD. Substitute GE = FD into (i): AB/BD = AE/FD, as required.

runtime_row.subject: Maths
runtime_row.questionText:
Case study: A right triangle ABC is right-angled at B. The largest square BRSP is inscribed in the triangle with one side along BC, one along BA and the opposite vertex S lying on the hypotenuse AC. Let AB = 16 cm and BC = 8 cm. Answer:
(i) Which similarity criterion relates △APS and △ABC, where P is on AB and S is on AC?
(ii) Set up the equation for the side x of the inscribed square BRSP using the similarity.
(iii) Solve for x.
(iv) State the side length of the largest inscribed square.
runtime_row.answer: (i) AA similarity: △APS and △ABC share ∠A, and ∠APS = ∠ABC = 90° (since PS is parallel to BC, being a side of the square). So △APS ~ △ABC by AA. (ii) Let the square's side be x cm. Then PB = x (a side of the square), so AP = AB − PB = 16 − x. Also PS = x. From △APS ~ △ABC: AP/AB = PS/BC, i.e., (16 − x)/16 = x/8. (iii) Cross-multiply: 8(16 − x) = 16x ⇒ 128 − 8x = 16x ⇒ 128 = 24x ⇒ x = 128/24 = 16/3 cm. (iv) Side of the largest inscribed square = 16/3 cm.
solutionSteps: (i) △APS and △ABC: ∠A is common; PS is a side of the square parallel to BC, so ∠APS = ∠ABC = 90°. By AA similarity, △APS ~ △ABC.
(ii) Let square side = x. PB = x (square side along BA), so AP = 16 − x. PS = x (square side opposite). Similarity ratio AP/AB = PS/BC gives (16 − x)/16 = x/8.
(iv) Side length of the largest inscribed square = 16/3 cm.
runtime_row.finalAnswer: (i) AA similarity. (ii) (16 − x)/16 = x/8. (iii) x = 16/3 cm. (iv) Side = 16/3 cm.
runtime_row.strategyHint: Inscribed square shares a corner with the right angle; the opposite corner on the hypotenuse gives the similar smaller triangle.

runtime_row.questionText:
Case study: The hypotenuse of a right triangle is 25 cm, and out of the two legs, one is longer than the other by 5 cm. Answer:
(i) Form a quadratic equation in the shorter leg x.
(ii) Solve the quadratic equation.
(iii) Reject the inadmissible root and state both legs.
(iv) Verify by computing x² + (x + 5)² and comparing with 25².
runtime_row.answer: (i) Let the shorter leg be x cm. Then the longer leg is (x + 5) cm. By Pythagoras: x² + (x + 5)² = 25² ⇒ x² + x² + 10x + 25 = 625 ⇒ 2x² + 10x − 600 = 0 ⇒ x² + 5x − 300 = 0. (ii) Solve x² + 5x − 300 = 0: split 5x = 20x − 15x (since 20 × (−15) = −300 and 20 + (−15) = 5), so x² + 20x − 15x − 300 = 0 ⇒ (x − 15)(x + 20) = 0. So x = 15 or x = −20. (iii) Length cannot be negative, so reject x = −20. Hence the shorter leg = 15 cm and the longer leg = 15 + 5 = 20 cm. (iv) Verification: x² + (x + 5)² = 15² + 20² = 225 + 400 = 625 = 25² ✓.
solutionSteps: (i) Shorter leg = x; longer leg = x + 5; hypotenuse = 25. Pythagoras: x² + (x + 5)² = 25².
(iii) Length > 0 ⇒ reject x = −20. Take x = 15 cm. Other leg = 15 + 5 = 20 cm.
runtime_row.strategyHint: Set up Pythagoras → quadratic in the shorter leg → factorise → reject negative root → verify.

(iii) How far from the base of the pole should the stake be driven so that the wire is taut? (Use Pythagoras.)
(iv) If a second guy wire 30 m long is used from the same top, what would be the new distance of the stake from the base?
runtime_row.answer: (i) The pole is vertical and the ground is horizontal, so the right angle is at the base of the pole. (ii) The guy wire (the slant side opposite the right angle) is the hypotenuse. (iii) Let the stake be x m from the base. By Pythagoras: x² + 18² = 24² ⇒ x² = 576 − 324 = 252 ⇒ x = √252 = 6√7 m ≈ 15.87 m. (iv) With a 30 m wire: x² + 18² = 30² ⇒ x² = 900 − 324 = 576 ⇒ x = 24 m.

(ii) Hypotenuse = side opposite the right angle = the guy wire.
(iii) Apply Pythagoras: (stake distance)² + (pole height)² = (wire length)². Let stake distance = x. x² + 18² = 24² ⇒ x² = 576 − 324 = 252 ⇒ x = 6√7 m ≈ 15.87 m.
runtime_row.finalAnswer: (i) At the base of the pole. (ii) The guy wire. (iii) 6√7 m ≈ 15.87 m. (iv) 24 m.

runtime_row.subject: Maths
runtime_row.questionText:
Assertion (A): The angle of elevation of the sun decreases as the height of the shadow increases.
Reason (R): As the angle of elevation θ decreases, tanθ decreases, so for the same object height, the shadow length (base) increases.
options: (A) Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
(B) Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion.
(C) Assertion is true but Reason is false.
(D) Assertion is false but Reason is true.
runtime_row.answer: (A) Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
solutionSteps: Assertion: When the sun is lower in the sky (smaller angle of elevation), shadows are longer. As shadow length increases, the angle of elevation of the sun decreases. TRUE.
Reason: tanθ = height/shadow length. For fixed height, if tanθ decreases (θ decreases), shadow length = height/tanθ increases. TRUE.
R explains the mathematical relationship behind A.
Answer: (A)
runtime_row.explanation: Both true. tanθ = height/shadow. Smaller θ → smaller tanθ → longer shadow. R correctly explains why the sun's lower angle of elevation gives longer shadows.

runtime_row.questionText: (A) A straight highway leads to the foot of a tower. A man standing on the top of the 75 m high tower observes two cars at angles of depression of 30o and 60o, which are approaching the foot of the tower. If one car is exactly behind the other on the same side of the tower, find the distance between the two cars. (use 3 = 1.73) 5 OR (B) From the top of a 7 m high building, the angle of elevation of the top of a cable tower is 60o and the angle of depression of its foot is 30o. Determine the height of the tower.
runtime_row.answer: (A) Distance between the two cars = 50√3 m = 86.5 m. (B) Height of the cable tower = 28 m.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] (A) Diagram: vertical tower AB = 75 m with foot A; the two cars at P and Q on the same horizontal line, with angles of depression 60° (nearer car P) and 30° (farther car Q) from the top B.
[1 mark] For the nearer car: in right triangle APB, tan 60° = AB/AP ⟹ √3 = 75/AP ⟹ AP = 75/√3 = 25√3 m.
[1 mark] For the farther car: in right triangle AQB, tan 30° = AB/AQ ⟹ 1/√3 = 75/AQ ⟹ AQ = 75√3 m.
[1 mark] Distance between the cars PQ = AQ − AP = 75√3 − 25√3 = 50√3 m.
[1 mark] Using √3 = 1.73, PQ = 50 × 1.73 = 86.5 m. (OR (B): height of cable tower = 28 m.)
runtime_row.finalAnswer: Distance between the two cars = 50√3 m ≈ 86.5 m. (OR (B): height of the tower = 28 m.)

runtime_row.questionText: One observer estimates the angle of elevation to the basket of a hot air balloon to be 60°, while another observer, standing 100 m away from the first on the opposite side of the balloon, estimates the angle of elevation to be 30°. Find : (a) The height of the basket from the ground. (b) The distance of the basket from the first observer. (c) The horizontal distance of the second observer from the basket.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] Diagram: basket B at height h vertically above point A on the ground; first observer at D (elevation 60°) and second observer at C (elevation 30°) on opposite sides of A, with DC = 100 m. Let DA = x, so AC = 100 − x.
[1 mark] For the first observer: tan 60° = h/x ⟹ √3 = h/x ⟹ h = x√3.  ...(i)
[1 mark] For the second observer: tan 30° = h/(100 − x) ⟹ 1/√3 = h/(100 − x) ⟹ 100 − x = h√3.  ...(ii)
[1 mark] (b) Distance of basket from first observer BD = h/sin 60° = 25√3 ÷ (√3/2) = 50 m. (c) Horizontal distance of second observer from the basket AC = 100 − x = 75 m.
runtime_row.finalAnswer: (a) height of basket = 25√3 m ≈ 43.3 m; (b) distance of basket from first observer = 50 m; (c) horizontal distance of second observer = 75 m.

runtime_row.questionText:
One evening, Kaushik was in a park. Children were playing cricket. Birds were singing on a nearby tree of height 80 m. He observed a bird on the tree at an angle of elevation of 45°. When a sixer was hit, a ball flew through the tree frightening the bird to fly away. In 2 seconds, he observed the bird flying at the same height at an angle of elevation of 30° and the ball flying towards him at the same height at an angle of elevation of 60°.

Part (i) [1 mark]: At what distance from the foot of the tree was he observing the bird sitting on the tree?

Part (ii) [2 marks]: How far did the bird fly in the mentioned time? OR After hitting the tree, how far did the ball travel in the sky when Kaushik saw the ball?

Part (iii) [1 mark]: What is the speed of the bird in m/min if it had flown 20(√3 + 1) m?
runtime_row.answer: (i) 80 m. (ii) Bird flew 80(√3 − 1) m. OR Ball travelled 80(1 − 1/√3) m. (iii) Speed = 600(√3 + 1) m/min.
solutionSteps: Part (i): With elevation 45° and tree height 80 m, tan 45° = 80/CB ⇒ CB = 80 m.
Part (ii): When bird flies away, new elevation 30°. tan 30° = 80/CE ⇒ (1/√3) = 80/CE ⇒ CE = 80√3. Bird displacement AD = BE = CE − CB = 80√3 − 80 = 80(√3 − 1) m.
Part (ii) OR: For the ball with elevation 60°: tan 60° = 80/CG ⇒ √3 = 80/CG ⇒ CG = 80/√3. Ball travel after hitting tree = CB − CG = 80 − 80/√3 = 80(1 − 1/√3) m.
Part (iii): Distance flown = 20(√3 + 1) m in 2 s. Speed = (20(√3 + 1) / 2) m/s = 10(√3 + 1) m/s. Convert to m/min: × 60 ⇒ 600(√3 + 1) m/min.

runtime_row.questionText: Train Speed: Sarthak is stopped at a railroad crossing. He spots a large oak tree beside the track some distance away and figures the angle between the track and his line to the tree (the angle of rotation from the crossing to the tree) is about 60 deg. His car is 40 m from the crossing (perpendicular to the track) and it takes the train 3 sec to travel from the crossing to the tree. How fast is the train moving?
solutionSteps: [1 mark] The 40 m line from the car to the crossing is perpendicular to the track. The distance from the crossing to the tree along the track = 40 * tan 60 = 40 * sqrt(3) = 69.28 m.
[1 mark] The train covers 69.28 m in 3 s.
[1 mark] Speed = distance / time = 69.28 / 3 = 23.09 m/sec.

runtime_row.finalAnswer: Let distances from foot be x (for 30°) and y (for 45°). x=40/ tan30°=40√3; y=40/ tan45°=40. Distance = 40(√3 − 1) m.

runtime_row.questionText: Assertion (A): For any angle θ where defined, 1+tan²θ = sec²θ. Reason (R): Dividing sin²θ+cos²θ=1 by cos²θ gives tan²θ+1=sec²θ.
runtime_row.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
runtime_row.explanation: Direct derivation from Pythagorean identity.
solutionSteps: Assertion (A) states the trigonometric identity 1+tan²θ = sec²θ. This is a standard identity.; Reason (R) explains that dividing the fundamental identity sin²θ+cos²θ=1 by cos²θ gives tan²θ+1=sec²θ. [½]
Dividing sin²θ+cos²θ=1 by cos²θ (assuming cosθ ≠ 0) yields (sin²θ/cos²θ) + (cos²θ/cos²θ) = 1/cos²θ. [½]
This simplifies to tan²θ + 1 = sec²θ, which is exactly the assertion. Thus, R correctly explains A. [1]
runtime_row.finalAnswer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

solutionSteps: Each sector angle = 120° [1]
Arc of each sector = (120/360) × 2π × 7 = 14π/3 [1]

Slant height = original radius = 7 cm [1]

runtime_row.subject: Maths
runtime_row.questionText: AB and CD are two perpendicular diameters of a circle of radius 7 cm. Find the area of the shaded region formed by two opposite quadrants.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] Given: circle of radius r = 7 cm with perpendicular diameters AB and CD; the shaded region is made of two opposite quadrants.
[1 mark] Each quadrant subtends 90° at the centre, so area of one quadrant = (90/360) × πr² = (1/4)πr².
[1 mark] Area of one quadrant = (1/4) × (22/7) × 7² = (1/4) × 22 × 7 = 38.5 cm².
[1 mark] The two opposite quadrants are congruent, so the shaded area = 2 × area of one quadrant.

runtime_row.questionText: Two arithmetic progressions have the same common difference. The difference between their 100th terms is 100. What is the difference between their 1000th terms? Justify.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] Let the APs be a, a+d, … and a′, a′+d, … with the same common difference d.
[1 mark] 100th terms: a + 99d and a′ + 99d.
[1 mark] Their difference = (a + 99d) − (a′ + 99d) = a − a′, which is independent of the term number.
[1 mark] Given a − a′ = 100.
[1 mark] 1000th terms differ by (a + 999d) − (a′ + 999d) = a − a′ = 100.

runtime_row.questionText: Find the 20th term counted from the last term of the AP 3, 8, 13, …, 253.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] The AP is 3, 8, 13, …, 253 with common difference d = 5.
[1 mark] Reading from the last term, the effective common difference becomes −5.
[1 mark] nth term from the end = l − (n − 1)d, with l = 253.
[1 mark] 20th term from the end = 253 − (20 − 1)(5) = 253 − 95.
[1 mark] Hence the 20th term from the end is 158.

runtime_row.subtopic: Bonding in Carbon and Chemical Properties
runtime_row.questionText: Carbon exhibits unique properties like catenation and tetravalency. Using these properties, explain why carbon forms an enormous variety of compounds. Also, discuss how these properties relate to the structural diversity of carbon compounds.
runtime_row.answer: Tetravalency allows formation of 4 bonds with various elements, creating diverse functional groups. Catenation enables long chain/ring formation. Together they produce structural isomerism, chain isomerism, and positional isomerism, resulting in enormous variety of compounds.
solutionSteps: 1. Tetravalency of Carbon:
- 4 valence electrons enable formation of 4 covalent bonds
- Can bond with C, H, O, N, S, P, halogens
- Allows diverse functional groups: -OH, -NH₂, -COOH, -CHO, etc.
2. Catenation:
- C-C bond is strong and stable
- Forms long chains and rings
- Chains can be straight, branched, or cyclic
3. Structural Diversity:
- Chain isomerism: Different arrangements of same formula
Example: C₅H₁₂ has 3 isomers (pentane, isopentane, neopentane)
- Position isomerism: Functional group at different positions
Example: CH₃CH₂CHO vs CH₃COCH₃ (both C₃H₆O)
- Functional group isomerism: Different functional groups
4. Result: Millions of organic compounds possible
From simple (CH₄) to complex (proteins, DNA)
runtime_row.finalAnswer: Tetravalency allows formation of 4 bonds with various elements, creating diverse functional groups. Catenation enables long chain/ring formation. Together they produce structural isomerism, chain isomerism, and positional isomerism, resulting in enormous variety of compounds.

runtime_row.subject: Science
runtime_row.questionText:
Consider the reaction between sodium and chlorine: 2Na + Cl₂ → 2NaCl

(a) Draw electron dot structure showing electron transfer.
(b) Identify which reactant is oxidized and which is reduced.
(c) Identify the oxidizing agent and reducing agent.
(d) Explain why this is a redox reaction.
(e) Calculate the number of electrons transferred when 23 g of sodium reacts.
solutionSteps: Write the balanced redox equation. Identify: (i) the substance oxidised — gains oxygen / loses hydrogen / loses electrons; (ii) the substance reduced — loses oxygen / gains hydrogen / gains electrons.
(a) Na loses 1e⁻: Na• → Na⁺ + e⁻
Cl gains 1e⁻: :Cl: + e⁻ → Cl⁻
(b) Na is oxidized (0→+1, loses e⁻)
Cl₂ is reduced (0→-1, gains e⁻)
(c) Reducing agent: Na (causes reduction by losing e⁻)
Oxidizing agent: Cl₂ (causes oxidation by gaining e⁻)
(d) Redox because: oxidation state change + electron transfer
(e) Molar mass of Na = 23 g/mol
23 g Na = 1 mol
From equation: 2 mol Na → 2 e⁻ transferred (1e⁻ per Na)
So 1 mol Na → 1 mol e⁻ = 6.022×10²³ electrons

(a) Find the length of each chord.
(b) Which chord is longer and why?
runtime_row.answer: (a) The chord at 4 cm from the centre is 6 cm; the chord at 3 cm is 8 cm. (b) The chord closer to the centre (3 cm away) is longer.
runtime_row.explanation: Chord length = 2√(r² − d²). For d = 4: 2√(25 − 16) = 6 cm. For d = 3: 2√(25 − 9) = 8 cm. The closer chord subtends a larger arc and is longer.

Length of chord at 4 cm is 2 * 3 = 6 cm. [1]
For chord at 3 cm: (half length)² = 5² - 3² = 16. Half length = 4 cm. Length = 8 cm. [1]
The chord at 3 cm (8 cm) is longer than the chord at 4 cm (6 cm) as it is closer to the centre. [1]
runtime_row.strategyHint: Remember the relationship between distance from the centre and chord length.
runtime_row.finalAnswer: (a) The chord at 4 cm from the centre is 6 cm; the chord at 3 cm is 8 cm. (b) The chord closer to the centre (3 cm away) is longer.

runtime_row.subject: Maths
runtime_row.questionText: Construct a configuration consisting of a circle of radius 6 cm and an external point P from which the two tangents are perpendicular to each other. Find OP, the tangent length, and verify your construction.
solutionSteps: If the two tangents are perpendicular, the angle between them is 90°. So the half-angle at P is 45°.
In the right triangle formed by O, the point of contact and P: sin 45° = r/OP ⇒ OP = 6/sin 45° = 6√2 cm.
Tangent length = OP × cos 45° = 6√2 × (√2/2) = 6 cm.
Verification: r² + (tangent)² = OP² ⇒ 36 + 36 = 72 = (6√2)². ✓
runtime_row.finalAnswer: Design: r = 6 cm, OP = 6√2 cm, tangent length = 6 cm.

runtime_row.questionText: Three consecutive vertices of a parallelogram ABCD taken in order are A(1, 2), B(4, 3) and C(6, 6). Using the property that the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, find the coordinates of the fourth vertex D.
runtime_row.answer: In a parallelogram the diagonals AC and BD bisect each other, so midpoint of AC = midpoint of BD. Midpoint of AC = ((1+6)/2, (2+6)/2) = (7/2, 4). Let D = (x, y); midpoint of BD = ((4+x)/2, (3+y)/2). Equate: (4+x)/2 = 7/2 ⇒ x = 3; (3+y)/2 = 4 ⇒ y = 5. So D = (3, 5). Check: AB = C−D vector: B−A = (3, 1) and C−D = (3, 1), confirming AB ∥ = DC.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] Property: diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other ⇒ midpoint of diagonal AC = midpoint of diagonal BD.
[1 mark] Let D = (x, y). Midpoint of BD = ((4+x)/2, (3+y)/2).
[1 mark] Equate x: (4+x)/2 = 7/2 ⇒ x = 3. Equate y: (3+y)/2 = 4 ⇒ y = 5.
[1 mark] D = (3, 5). Verify: B−A = (3, 1) and C−D = (3, 1) so AB ∥ = DC. Hence ABCD is a parallelogram.
runtime_row.strategyHint: For a parallelogram, set midpoint of one diagonal equal to midpoint of the other and solve.

runtime_row.questionText: Find the ratio in which the x-axis divides the line segment joining the points A(2, −3) and B(5, 6). Also find the coordinates of the point of division and its distance from the origin.
runtime_row.answer: Let the x-axis divide AB in ratio k : 1. Its y-coordinate is 0, so by section formula y = (6k + (−3)·1)/(k+1) = 0 ⇒ 6k − 3 = 0 ⇒ k = 1/2, giving ratio 1 : 2. x-coordinate: x = (1·5 + 2·2)/(1+2) = (5+4)/3 = 3. Point of division = (3, 0). Distance from origin = √(3²+0²) = 3 units.

[1 mark] Point of division = (3, 0).
[1 mark] Distance from the origin = √(3² + 0²) = 3 units.

runtime_row.subject: Science
runtime_row.questionText: Explain Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment with a dihybrid cross involving seed color (yellow-dominant, green-recessive) and seed shape (round-dominant, wrinkled-recessive). Show the Punnett square and explain how the 9:3:3:1 ratio proves independent assortment. How would the ratio change if the genes were linked?
runtime_row.answer: 9:3:3:1 ratio proves independent assortment; linked genes show deviation with parental phenotypes more frequent
solutionSteps: Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment: alleles of different genes assort independently during gamete formation.
Parental cross: AABB (yellow round) × aabb (green wrinkled)
F₁: All AaBb (yellow round)
F₁ × F₁: AaBb × AaBb
Gamete types: AB, Ab, aB, ab (4 types from each parent)
Punnett square: 16 boxes showing all combinations
Phenotypic ratio: 9:3:3:1
9 A_B_: yellow round (both dominant)
3 A_bb: yellow wrinkled (seed color dominant)
3 aaB_: green round (seed shape dominant)
1 aabb: green wrinkled (both recessive)
If genes linked: Lower recombination types, higher parental types
Example: 11:1:1:3 or other deviations from 9:3:3:1
runtime_row.finalAnswer: 9:3:3:1 ratio proves independent assortment; linked genes show deviation with parental phenotypes more frequent

runtime_row.subject: Science
runtime_row.questionText:
Study the following cross showing self pollination in F1; fill in the blank and answer the question that follows.
Parents: RRYY × rryy (Round, yellow × wrinkled, green)
F1: RrYy × ?
(Round, yellow)
runtime_row.answer: The blank is RrYy. F1 plants (all RrYy, round-yellow) are self-pollinated, meaning each F1 plant is crossed with itself (genotype RrYy). So the cross is RrYy × RrYy. Each F1 plant produces four kinds of gametes (RY, Ry, rY, ry) in equal proportions. Self-pollination of RrYy × RrYy gives the classic Mendelian dihybrid F2 distribution of 9:3:3:1 (round-yellow : round-green : wrinkled-yellow : wrinkled-green).
solutionSteps: F1 genotype = RrYy (all round, yellow).
'Self pollination' means F1 is crossed with itself → the missing parent is RrYy.
Each RrYy plant produces 4 gametes — RY, Ry, rY, ry — in equal numbers.
RrYy × RrYy produces 16 combinations in F2 (Punnett 4×4).
The phenotype distribution is the classic dihybrid ratio 9:3:3:1.
So the blank is 'RrYy' (the F1 plant itself being selfed).
runtime_row.finalAnswer: The blank is RrYy — F1 (RrYy) is self-pollinated → RrYy × RrYy gives 9:3:3:1 in F2.
runtime_row.strategyHint: Self-pollination = cross with itself → the missing parent has the same genotype as F1.

runtime_row.subject: Science
runtime_row.questionText:
Given below are certain situations. Analyse and describe its possible impact on a person:
(a) Testes of a male boy are not able to descend into scrotum during his embryonic development.
(b) Vas deferens of a man is plugged.
(c) Prostate and seminal vesicles are not functional.
(d) Egg is not fertilised in a human female.
(e) Placenta does not attach to the uterus optimally.

[OR]

(a) A doctor has advised Sameer to reduce sugar intake in his diet and do regular exercise after checking his blood test reports. Which disease do you think Sameer is suffering from? Name the hormone responsible for this disease and the organ producing the hormone.
(b) Which hormone is present in the areas of rapid cell division in a plant and which hormone inhibits the growth?
runtime_row.answer: Main: anatomy/physiology impacts (a–e listed). OR Alt: (a) Diabetes; Insulin; Pancreas. (b) Cytokinins promote cell division; Abscisic acid inhibits growth.
solutionSteps: (a) Sperm formation will be adversely affected because spermatogenesis requires a temperature lower than core body temperature (the scrotum keeps testes ~2 °C cooler). Undescended testes → reduced or absent sperm production.
(b) Vas deferens is the passage for sperm transfer from testis to urethra. If plugged, sperms cannot be transferred further — leading to infertility despite normal sperm production.
(c) Prostate gland and seminal vesicles produce secretions that nourish sperm and form the medium (semen) for sperm transport. If non-functional, sperms lack nourishment and proper transport medium.

(d) If the egg is not fertilised, it lives for about one day. Then the thickened lining of the uterus breaks, leading to discharge of blood and mucus along with the unfertilised egg — this is called menstruation.
(e) Placenta provides nutrition and oxygen to the growing embryo. Sub-optimal attachment will impair nutrition and oxygen supply, affecting embryo growth and possibly causing serious complications.
OR (alternative): (a) Diabetes; hormone = Insulin; organ = Pancreas. (b) Cytokinins are present in regions of rapid cell division and promote it; Abscisic acid inhibits growth.
runtime_row.finalAnswer: Main: (a)–(e) impacts described. OR Alt: Diabetes/Insulin/Pancreas; Cytokinins/Abscisic acid.

runtime_row.subject: Science
runtime_row.questionText: Assertion (A): The umbilical cord connects the fetus directly to the mother's blood vessels. Reason (R): The umbilical cord contains blood vessels for nutrient and waste exchange.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.
runtime_row.answer: D. A is false, R is true.
solutionSteps: The umbilical cord connects the fetus to the placenta, not directly to the mother's blood vessels — A is false.
Fetal and maternal blood do NOT directly mix; the placenta acts as a barrier and exchange occurs across the placental membrane.
The umbilical cord contains blood vessels (umbilical arteries and vein) that carry nutrients, oxygen and wastes between the fetus and the placenta — R is true.
Hence A is false, R is true.
runtime_row.finalAnswer: D. A is false, R is true.
runtime_row.explanation: The Assertion is false: the umbilical cord connects the fetus to the placenta, and fetal blood never joins the mother's blood vessels directly — exchange takes place across the placental membrane. The Reason is true: the umbilical cord contains blood vessels that carry nutrients, oxygen and wastes between the fetus and the placenta. Hence A is false, R is true.

runtime_row.subject: Science
runtime_row.questionText: Compare asexual and sexual reproduction in terms of genetic variation and adaptability to environmental changes.
runtime_row.answer: Asexual reproduction produces genetically identical offspring with no variation, making species less adaptable. Sexual reproduction creates genetic variation through combination of parental genes, enabling better adaptation to environmental changes and evolution.
solutionSteps: Asexual Reproduction:
- Involves one parent
- No genetic recombination
- All offspring are clones (genetically identical)
- No variation means limited adaptability
- Vulnerable to same diseases/environmental stress
Sexual Reproduction:
- Involves two parents
- Genetic recombination during meiosis
- High genetic variation among offspring
- Variation allows better adaptability
- Some offspring may survive environmental changes
Evolutionary advantage of sexual reproduction through genetic diversity.
runtime_row.finalAnswer: Asexual reproduction produces genetically identical offspring with no variation, making species less adaptable. Sexual reproduction creates genetic variation through combination of parental genes, enabling better adaptation to environmental changes and evolution.

runtime_row.subject: Science
runtime_row.questionText:
A 45-year-old man visits an optometrist complaining that he cannot read small print on his mobile phone but can see distant objects clearly. However, 10 years ago, he could read small print comfortably.

(i) Identify the vision defect and explain its cause.
(ii) What optical device(s) can correct this defect?
(iii) The man is also a pilot. Explain why his condition might require special consideration.
(iv) Calculate the power of the lens needed if the man's near point is 50 cm and the normal near point is 25 cm.
(v) Discuss whether his distant vision should be corrected along with near vision correction.
runtime_row.answer: Presbyopia; loss of lens elasticity with age; bifocal/progressive lenses needed; critical for pilot safety; Power = 2D; bifocal correction required for both near and far vision.
solutionSteps: (i) The defect is presbyopia. With age, the lens loses elasticity and the ciliary muscles weaken. This reduces the eye's ability to accommodate for near objects while distant vision remains normal.
(ii) Bifocal or progressive lenses: upper part for distant vision (no power or weak), lower part for near vision (convex lens). Alternatively, separate spectacles for near and far viewing.

(iii) As a pilot, clear vision at both near and distant ranges is critical for instrument reading and external observation. Presbyopia might affect his ability to read instruments while maintaining awareness of surroundings.

(v) Yes, bifocal or progressive lenses are recommended. The upper portion provides no correction (or weak convex lens) for distant vision, while the lower portion has +2D for near vision. This allows him to see clearly at all distances, which is essential for his profession.
runtime_row.finalAnswer: Presbyopia; loss of lens elasticity with age; bifocal/progressive lenses needed; critical for pilot safety; Power = 2D; bifocal correction required for both near and far vision.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

runtime_row.answer: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

It receives oxygenated blood from lungs

runtime_row.subject: Science
runtime_row.questionText:
Case Study: Rahul visited an eye doctor and was told he has myopia (short-sightedness). His prescription says: Power = −2.5 D. His friend Priya has hypermetropia (long-sightedness) with Power = +1.5 D.

Part (i) [1 mark]: What type of lens is used to correct myopia? What does the negative sign in Rahul's prescription indicate?

Part (ii) [1 mark]: Calculate the focal length of Priya's lens. What type of lens is it and why is it used for hypermetropia?

Part (iii) [2 marks]: If Rahul's doctor combines both lenses together (in contact), what is the combined power? What defect can this combination correct? Also state the lens formula and define its terms.
runtime_row.answer: Part (i): Concave lens corrects myopia. The negative sign indicates it is a concave (diverging) lens with focal length −40 cm. Part (ii): f = 66.7 cm. Convex lens. Used because it converges light to form image on retina. Part (iii): Combined P = −1.0 D (concave). Can correct mild myopia. Lens formula: 1/v − 1/u = 1/f.
solutionSteps: Part (i):
Myopia (short-sightedness): image forms in front of retina
Correction: a concave (diverging) lens is used
Concave lens diverges light rays before they enter the eye
This shifts the image back onto the retina
Negative power (−2.5 D): indicates a concave lens
Focal length: f = 1/P = 1/(−2.5) = −0.4 m = −40 cm
Therefore: concave lens; negative sign means diverging lens with f = −40 cm
Part (ii):
Power P = +1.5 D
Focal length f = 1/P = 1/1.5 = 0.667 m = 66.7 cm
Positive power → convex (converging) lens
Hypermetropia: image forms behind the retina
Convex lens converges light before entering eye
This brings the image forward onto the retina
Therefore f = 66.7 cm; convex lens corrects hypermetropia by converging light
Part (iii):
Combined power of lenses in contact:
Combined focal length: f = 1/P = 1/(−1.0) = −1.0 m = −100 cm
A combined power of −1.0 D is a concave lens
This can correct mild myopia (short-sightedness)
Lens formula: 1/v − 1/u = 1/f
Where:
v = image distance (from optical centre of lens)
u = object distance (from optical centre of lens)
f = focal length of lens
Sign convention: distances measured from optical centre; positive to the right, negative to the left
Therefore combined P = −1.0 D (corrects mild myopia); lens formula: 1/v − 1/u = 1/f
runtime_row.finalAnswer: Part (i): Concave lens. Negative sign = concave (diverging) lens, f = −40 cm. Part (ii): f = 66.7 cm; Convex lens converges light to correct hypermetropia. Part (iii): P = −1.0 D (concave, corrects mild myopia). Lens formula: 1/v − 1/u = 1/f.
runtime_row.explanation: Part (i): Myopia corrected by concave lens. Negative power means concave lens. f = 1/P = 1/(−2.5) = −40 cm. Part (ii): f = 1/1.5 = 0.667 m = 66.7 cm. Convex (positive power) lens converges light, correcting hypermetropia where image forms behind retina. Part (iii): P = −2.5 + 1.5 = −1.0 D. Combined lens is concave, corrects mild myopia. Lens formula: 1/v − 1/u = 1/f.

runtime_row.questionText: In an experiment to trace the path of a ray of light through a glass prism for different values of angle of incidence a student would find that the emergent ray:
options: Is parallel to the incident ray.
Is parallel to the refracted ray.
Bends at an angle to the direction of incident ray.
runtime_row.answer: Bends at an angle to the direction of incident ray.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] Unlike a glass slab, the two refracting surfaces of a prism are NOT parallel, so the two bendings do not cancel: the emergent ray is deviated at an angle (the angle of deviation) to the direction of the incident ray.
runtime_row.finalAnswer: Bends at an angle to the direction of incident ray.

runtime_row.subject: Science
runtime_row.questionText: In an experiment to trace the path of a ray of light through a triangular glass prism, a student would observe that the emergent ray.
options: Is parallel to the incident ray.
Is along the same direction of incident ray.
Gets deviated and bends towards the thinner part of the prism.
Gets deviated and bends towards the thicker part (base) of the prism.
runtime_row.answer: Gets deviated and bends towards the thicker part (base) of the prism.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] Because the prism's refracting surfaces are inclined to each other and glass is denser than air, the ray bends towards the base at both refractions; the net deviation of the emergent ray is always towards the thicker part (base) of the prism.
runtime_row.finalAnswer: Gets deviated and bends towards the thicker part (base) of the prism.

runtime_row.questionText: A student traces the path of a ray of light through a triangular glass prism for different values of angle of incidence. On analysing the ray diagrams, which one of the following conclusions is he likely to draw?
options: The emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray.
The emergent ray bends at an angle to the direction of the incident ray.
The emergent ray and the refracted ray are at right angles to each other.
The emergent ray is perpendicular to the incident ray.
runtime_row.answer: The emergent ray bends at an angle to the direction of the incident ray.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] In a prism the refracting surfaces are inclined, so the deviations at the two faces add instead of cancelling; the emergent ray is always deviated at an angle (the angle of deviation) to the incident ray - it is never parallel to it.
runtime_row.finalAnswer: The emergent ray bends at an angle to the direction of the incident ray.

runtime_row.questionText: A camera uses a converging lens of focal length 5 cm to form images of objects at different distances. (a) If an object at distance 20 cm is to be photographed, calculate the image distance and magnification. (b) What happens to the image when the object is moved closer to the lens? (c) Explain why adjusting the position of the film (sensor) is necessary when photographing objects at different distances. (d) Design an optical system that can photograph both near and distant objects clearly.
runtime_row.answer: Image at 6.67cm, magnification -0.33; Image moves farther as object approaches; Focus adjustment needed; Use autofocus or variable aperture
solutionSteps: (a) f = 5 cm, u = 20 cm (object beyond 2f = 10 cm)
m = -v/u = -6.67/20 = -0.33 (diminished inverted)
(b) As object approaches lens, image distance increases (moves away from lens)
When u approaches f = 5 cm: v approaches infinity
(c) Since v depends on u through lens formula, different object distances require different image distances
The sensor/film must be at image distance for sharp focus
(d) Autofocus systems use sensors to detect focus and adjust lens position; Variable aperture increases depth of field
runtime_row.finalAnswer: Image at 6.67cm, magnification -0.33; Image moves farther as object approaches; Focus adjustment needed; Use autofocus or variable aperture

runtime_row.questionText: Which of the following statement is not correct about two parallel conductors carrying equal currents in the same direction?
options: Each conductor exerts a force on the other.
The two conductors will repel each other.
There are concentric lines of force around each conductor.
Each of the conductors will move if not prevented from doing so.
runtime_row.answer: The two conductors will repel each other.
solutionSteps: Parallel conductors carrying currents in the same direction attract each other (each lies in the other's magnetic field and experiences a force); there are concentric field lines around each, and each will move if free. So the statement that is NOT correct is (b) 'The two conductors will repel each other'.
runtime_row.finalAnswer: (b) The two conductors will repel each other.

runtime_row.subject: Science
runtime_row.question: Explain briefly the process of electrolytic reduction used in the extraction of aluminium. Why is cryolite added to the electrolyte?
runtime_row.answer: Aluminium oxide is dissolved in molten cryolite and electrolysed. At the cathode, Al³⁺ ions gain electrons to form molten aluminium. Cryolite lowers the melting point and increases conductivity of the mixture, making the process economical.
runtime_row.explanation: Pure alumina has a very high melting point; dissolving it in cryolite reduces the temperature required and improves ion mobility.
solutionSteps: Aluminium oxide (alumina) is dissolved in molten cryolite to form the electrolyte.; During electrolysis, Al³⁺ ions migrate to the cathode and gain electrons to form molten aluminium (Al³⁺ + 3e⁻ → Al). [1]
Cryolite is added because it significantly lowers the melting point of alumina from 2072°C to about 900°C.; It also increases the electrical conductivity of the electrolyte mixture. [1]
These effects make the electrolytic reduction process more energy-efficient and economical. [1]
runtime_row.finalAnswer: Aluminium oxide is dissolved in molten cryolite and electrolysed. At the cathode, Al³⁺ ions gain electrons to form molten aluminium. Cryolite lowers the melting point and increases conductivity of the mixture, making the process economical.

runtime_row.question: Name the main step used to extract iron from hematite in the blast furnace. Describe briefly.
runtime_row.answer: Reduction of iron oxide by carbon monoxide in the blast furnace.
runtime_row.explanation: In the blast furnace, carbon monoxide reduces Fe₂O₃ to molten iron: Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂.
solutionSteps: The main step used to extract iron from hematite in the blast furnace is reduction.; In the blast furnace, carbon monoxide (CO) acts as the primary reducing agent. [½]
Carbon monoxide reduces iron oxide (Fe2O3) to molten iron (Fe). [½]
This reduction occurs at high temperatures, removing oxygen from the ore. [1]
runtime_row.finalAnswer: Reduction of iron oxide by carbon monoxide in the blast furnace.

runtime_row.subject: Maths
runtime_row.questionText:
The sum of a two digit number and the number obtained by reversing the digits is 66. If the digits of the number differ by 2, find the number. How many such numbers are there?

[OR]

Solve: 2/√x + 3/√y = 2 ; 4/√x − 9/√y = −1, x, y > 0.
runtime_row.answer: Main: The numbers are 42 and 24 (two such numbers). OR Alt: x = 4, y = 9.
solutionSteps: Let tens digit = x, units digit = y. Original number = 10x + y; reversed number = 10y + x. Sum: (10x + y) + (10y + x) = 66 ⇒ 11(x + y) = 66 ⇒ x + y = 6.
Digits differ by 2: either x − y = 2 or y − x = 2.
Case 1: x + y = 6 and x − y = 2 ⇒ x = 4, y = 2 → number = 42. Case 2: x + y = 6 and y − x = 2 ⇒ x = 2, y = 4 → number = 24. Two such numbers: 42 and 24.
OR (alternative): Let 1/√x = m, 1/√y = n. Equations become 2m + 3n = 2 and 4m − 9n = −1. Multiply first by −2: −4m − 6n = −4. Add to second: −15n = −5 ⇒ n = 1/3. Substitute: 2m + 1 = 2 ⇒ m = 1/2.
runtime_row.finalAnswer: Main: 42 and 24 (two numbers). OR Alt: x = 4, y = 9.

runtime_row.questionText: Two angles are supplementary. The larger angle is 6° less than twice the smaller angle. Find the two angles.
runtime_row.answer: The angles are 118° and 62°. Let larger = x, smaller = y. Then x + y = 180 and x = 2y − 6. Solving gives y = 62, x = 118.

runtime_row.questionText: The measures of two complementary angles are in the ratio 4 : 5. Find the measure of each angle.
runtime_row.answer: The angles are 40° and 50°. Let the angles be x and y with x/y = 4/5, so 5x = 4y, and x + y = 90 (complementary). Solving gives x = 40, y = 50.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] Let the two angles be x° and y°. Being complementary: x + y = 90 …(1).
[1 mark] Their measures are in the ratio 4 : 5, so x/y = 4/5 → 5x − 4y = 0 …(2).
[1 mark] From (1), y = 90 − x; substitute into (2): 5x − 4(90 − x) = 0 → 9x − 360 = 0 → x = 40.
[1 mark] Then y = 90 − 40 = 50.
[1 mark] Hence the angles are 40° and 50°. (Check: sum 90° ✓; 40 : 50 = 4 : 5 ✓.)

runtime_row.questionText:
The polynomial f(x) = x³ − 6x² + 11x − 6 models the profit (in lakh ₹, a negative value meaning a loss) of a small start-up x years after it opened.
(a) Factorise f(x) completely.
(b) Find the times at which the profit becomes zero (break-even).
(c) Discuss which of these times are meaningful.
runtime_row.answer: (a) f(x) = (x − 1)(x − 2)(x − 3). (b) The profit is zero at x = 1, 2 and 3 years. (c) All three zeros are positive, so all three are meaningful break-even times (a profit, unlike a population, may be negative in between).
runtime_row.explanation: By testing small integers, f(1) = f(2) = f(3) = 0. Grouping gives f(x) = (x − 1)(x² − 5x + 6) = (x − 1)(x − 2)(x − 3). The zeros are the break-even times; since they are all positive (x ≥ 0 is the valid domain), all three are meaningful. Negative times would not be meaningful.
solutionSteps: By trial, f(1) = 1 − 6 + 11 − 6 = 0. So (x − 1) is a factor. [1]
Profit is zero at x = 1, 2, 3 years. All are positive times, hence all are meaningful break-even points. [1]
runtime_row.strategyHint: Test small integer values to identify factors and relate roots to real‑world contexts.
runtime_row.finalAnswer: (a) f(x) = (x − 1)(x − 2)(x − 3). (b) x = 1, 2 and 3 years. (c) All three are positive, so all three are meaningful break-even times.

runtime_row.questionText:
f(x) = x³ - ax² + (a - 3)x + 6, where a is a non-zero real number. When f(x) is divided by (x + 1), there is no remainder.

If f(x) is completely factorisable, find the zeroes of f(x). Show your steps.
solutionSteps: [0.5 mark] Writes that, since f(x) is divisible by (x + 1), f(-1) = 0, and finds the value of a as 4.
[0.5 mark] Uses the above step and writes f(x) as x³ - 4x² + x + 6.

[1 mark] Since (x + 1) is a factor, writes f(x) = (x + 1)(x² + bx + c) and compares coefficients: b + 1 = -4 gives b = -5, and c = 6; the x-coefficient checks as c + b = 6 - 5 = 1. The quotient is therefore x² - 5x + 6.
[0.5 mark] Factorises the quotient as (x - 2)(x - 3).
[0.5 mark] Finds the zeroes of f(x) as (-1), 2 and 3.
runtime_row.finalAnswer: a = 4 and the zeroes of f(x) are -1, 2 and 3.

One zero of f(x) = x³ - 3x² + 4 is 2.

At how many points will the graph of f(x) intersect the x-axis? Show your steps.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] Since 2 is a zero, (x - 2) is a factor. Writes f(x) = (x - 2)(x² + bx + c) and compares coefficients: b - 2 = -3 gives b = -1, and -2c = 4 gives c = -2; the x-coefficient checks as c - 2b = -2 + 2 = 0. The quotient is therefore x² - x - 2.
[0.5 mark] Factorises the quotient as (x - 2)(x + 1).
[0.5 mark] Concludes from the above step that the graph of f(x) intersects the x-axis at two points, since f(x) = (x - 2)²(x + 1) has only the two distinct zeroes 2 and -1.

runtime_row.questionText:
A carton has 24 bulbs of which 6 are defective. One bulb is drawn at random; this bulb is NOT replaced. Then a second bulb is drawn at random from the remainder.
(i) What is the probability that the FIRST bulb drawn is NOT defective?
(ii) Given that the first bulb is defective, what is the probability that the second bulb is also defective?
(iii) Given that the first bulb is defective, how many bulbs remain and how many are defective?
(iv) Why is the second probability conditional on the first event?
solutionSteps: (i) Good bulbs = 24 − 6 = 18. P(first bulb good) = 18/24 = 3/4.
(ii) After removing one defective, 23 bulbs remain with 5 defective. P(second defective) = 5/23.
(iii) Remaining bulbs = 23; defective bulbs remaining = 5.
(iv) Because the first bulb is NOT replaced, the sample space for the second draw depends on what happened in the first draw — that's the definition of conditional probability.
runtime_row.finalAnswer: (i) 3/4; (ii) 5/23; (iii) 23 bulbs, 5 defective; (iv) Because the first bulb is not replaced.

Model Rocketry: Shalvi launches a rocket from a large field. At the moment its fuel is exhausted, the rocket has a velocity of 240 ft/sec and an altitude of 544 ft. After t sec, its height h(t) above the ground is given by h(t) = -16t^2 + 240t + 544.
(i) How high is the rocket 5 sec after the fuel is exhausted?
(ii) How high is the rocket 10 sec after the fuel is exhausted?
(iii) How could the rocket be at the same height at t = 5 and at t = 10?
(iv) What is the maximum height attained by the rocket?
(v) How many seconds was the rocket airborne after its fuel was exhausted?
solutionSteps: [1 mark] (iii) The graph is a downward parabola symmetric about its vertex t = -240/(2 x -16) = 7.5 sec; t = 5 and t = 10 are equidistant from 7.5, so the rocket is at the same height (1344 ft) going up at t = 5 and coming down at t = 10.
[1 mark] (v) Airborne until h(t) = 0: -16t^2 + 240t + 544 = 0 => t^2 - 15t - 34 = 0 => (t - 17)(t + 2) = 0 => t = 17 (reject t = -2). The rocket was airborne 17 sec.
runtime_row.finalAnswer: (i) 1344 ft  (ii) 1344 ft  (iii) equal heights by parabolic symmetry about t = 7.5  (iv) 1444 ft  (v) 17 sec

Fencing a Backyard: Tina and Shriya have just purchased a German Shepherd and need to fence in their backyard so the dog can run.
(i) What is the maximum rectangular area they can enclose with 200 ft of fencing if they use fencing along all four sides? What are the dimensions of the rectangle?
(ii) What is the maximum area if they use the house as one of the sides? What are the dimensions of this rectangle?
solutionSteps: [1 mark] (i) Let width = x. With 2(length + width) = 200, length = 100 - x. Area A(x) = x(100 - x) = -(x - 50)^2 + 2500.
[1 mark] (i) A(x) is maximum at x = 50: maximum area = 2500 sq ft with dimensions 50 ft x 50 ft.
[1 mark] (ii) Using the house as one side, fencing covers one length and two widths: L + 2x = 200, so L = 200 - 2x. Area A(x) = x(200 - 2x) = -2(x - 50)^2 + 5000.
[1 mark] (ii) Maximum at x = 50: maximum area = 5000 sq ft with dimensions width 50 ft and length 100 ft.
runtime_row.finalAnswer: (i) max area 2500 sq ft, dimensions 50 ft x 50 ft  (ii) max area 5000 sq ft, dimensions 50 ft x 100 ft (house as one side)

runtime_row.questionText:
Building Sheep Pens: Darsh and Darpan are fencing off a large rectangular area to build holding pens. The large rectangle is partitioned into three smaller, equal-size pens by two internal fences parallel to the shorter side.
(i) If 384 ft of fencing is available and the maximum area is desired, what will be the dimensions of the larger, outer rectangle?
(ii) What will be the dimensions of the smaller holding pens?
solutionSteps: [1 mark] Let the outer rectangle have length L and width W, with 2 internal partitions parallel to the width. Total fencing = 2 lengths + 4 widths: 2L + 4W = 384, so L = 192 - 2W.
[1 mark] (i) Maximum at W = 48, giving L = 192 - 96 = 96. Outer rectangle dimensions: 48 ft by 96 ft.
[1 mark] (ii) The 96 ft length is split into 3 equal pens by the 2 partitions, so each smaller pen measures 48 ft by (96/3) = 32 ft.
runtime_row.finalAnswer: (i) outer rectangle 48 ft by 96 ft  (ii) each smaller pen 48 ft by 32 ft

runtime_row.questionText: The product of two consecutive positive odd integers is 483. Find the two integers.
runtime_row.answer: The consecutive positive odd integers are 21 and 23.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] Let the smaller odd integer be x; the next consecutive odd integer is x + 2. Given product: x(x + 2) = 483.
[1 mark] Write in standard form: x² + 2x − 483 = 0.
[1 mark] Split the middle term: x² + 23x − 21x − 483 = 0 ⇒ (x + 23)(x − 21) = 0.
[1 mark] Roots x = 21 or x = −23. Reject x = −23 because the integers must be positive.
[1 mark] So x = 21 and the integers are 21 and 23 (21 × 23 = 483 ✓).

runtime_row.subject: Maths
runtime_row.questionText: Check whether the statement below is true or false. "The square root of every composite number is rational." Justify your answer by proving rationality or irrationality as applicable.
runtime_row.answer: False. Counter-example: 6 is composite but √6 is irrational.
solutionSteps: Take a composite number that is not a perfect square — e.g. 6. Assume √6 = a/b with a, b co-prime, b ≠ 0.
Then 6b² = a² ⟹ 2 and 3 divide a², so 2 and 3 divide a ⟹ a = 6c. Substitute: 6b² = 36c² ⟹ b² = 6c², so 2 and 3 divide b. This contradicts co-prime assumption — √6 is irrational. Statement is false.
runtime_row.finalAnswer: False — √6 is irrational, so the square root of every composite number is NOT rational.

runtime_row.questionText:
Assertion (A): √3 + √5 is irrational.
Reason (R): The sum of two irrational numbers is always irrational.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, R is false.
A is false, R is true.
runtime_row.answer: A is true, R is false.
runtime_row.explanation: √3 + √5 is indeed irrational, but the reason is incorrect — for example, √2 + (−√2) = 0 is rational. R is a false generalisation.
solutionSteps: Assertion (A): Assume √3 + √5 = r (rational). Then √5 = r − √3. Squaring: 5 = r² − 2r√3 + 3, so 2r√3 = r² − 2, giving √3 = (r²−2)/(2r), which is rational — contradiction. So √3 + √5 is irrational. A is TRUE.
Reason (R): The sum of two irrational numbers is NOT always irrational. Counter-example: √2 + (−√2) = 0, which is rational. So R is FALSE.
Since A is true and R is false, the correct option is: A is true, R is false.
runtime_row.finalAnswer: A is true, R is false.

(Take pi = 22/7.) A sugar cone is 10 cm deep and has a diameter of 4 cm. A spherical scoop of ice cream with a diameter of 4 cm rests on top of the cone.
(i) If all the ice cream melts into the cone, will the cone overflow? Explain by comparing the two volumes.
(ii) If the cone does not overflow, what percent of the cone will be filled?
solutionSteps: [1 mark] Cone: radius r = 2 cm, height h = 10 cm. Volume of cone = (1/3)*pi*r^2*h = (1/3)*pi*4*10 = 40*pi/3 cm^3 (approx 41.9 cm^3).
[1 mark] (i) Sphere of ice cream: radius 2 cm. Volume = (4/3)*pi*r^3 = (4/3)*pi*8 = 32*pi/3 cm^3 (approx 33.5 cm^3).
[1 mark] (i) Since 32*pi/3 < 40*pi/3 (approx 33.5 cm^3 < 41.9 cm^3), the ice-cream volume is less than the cone volume, so the cone will NOT overflow.
[1 mark] (ii) Percent filled = (32*pi/3) / (40*pi/3) * 100 = (32/40)*100 = 80%. The cone will be about 80% filled.
runtime_row.finalAnswer: (i) No, it will not overflow (33.5 cm^3 < 41.9 cm^3)  (ii) about 80% filled

A photographer uses similar triangles to determine the height of a building. She stands 50 m away from the base of a building and holds a device that shows an angle of 60° to the top. She also uses a small scale model (ΔABC) with base 2 m and height 2√3 m (angle at base = 60°).

solutionSteps: Construction: Draw two similar right triangles — small model (base 2 m, height 2√3 m, 60° at base) and the building triangle (base 50 m, 60° at base, unknown height h). Label all given measurements and show the similarity correspondence.

(b) Both triangles have a right angle and 60° angle at base, so AA similarity holds
(c) From 100 m distance: tan(angle) = 50√3/100 = √3/2 ≈ 0.866

runtime_row.subject: Maths
runtime_row.questionText:
Assertion (A): Two right triangles with the same hypotenuse are always congruent.
Reason (R): If the hypotenuse and one side of a right triangle are equal to the hypotenuse and one side of another right triangle, then the two triangles are congruent (RHS).
options: (A) Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
(B) Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion.
(C) Assertion is true but Reason is false.
(D) Assertion is false but Reason is true.
runtime_row.answer: (D) Assertion is false but Reason is true.
solutionSteps: Assertion: Two right triangles with the same hypotenuse are NOT necessarily congruent — only if the hypotenuse AND one other side are equal (RHS congruence). With just the same hypotenuse, the triangles can have different side lengths. For example: hypotenuse = 5, sides (3,4) and (√7, √18) are both right triangles with hypotenuse 5 but different. FALSE.
Reason: RHS congruence criterion — hypotenuse + one side equal → congruent. This is a valid congruence criterion. TRUE.
A is false (hypotenuse alone insufficient), R is true (RHS requires hypotenuse AND one side).
Answer: (D)
runtime_row.explanation: A is false — same hypotenuse alone is insufficient for congruence (e.g., 3-4-5 and √7-√18-5 triangles). R is the correct RHS criterion which requires both hypotenuse AND one side to be equal.

runtime_row.questionText: From an external point P, the length of the tangent PA to a circle is 8 cm. The distance from the centre O to the external point P is 10 cm. Find the diameter of the circle.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] OA ⊥ AP (radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact). By Pythagoras Theorem, OP² = OA² + AP² → OA = √(10² − 8²) = √(100 − 64) = √36 = 6 cm = radius.
[1 mark] Diameter = 2r = 2 × 6 = 12 cm.

runtime_row.questionText: A(3, 0), B(6, 4) and C(–1, 3) are vertices of a triangle ABC. Find the length of its median BE.
runtime_row.answer: Midpoint of AC is E(1, 3/2). Length of median BE = √[(6 − 1)² + (4 − 3/2)²] = √(125/4) = 5√5/2 units.
solutionSteps: Median BE joins B to the midpoint E of AC: E = ((3 + (–1))/2, (0 + 3)/2) = (1, 3/2).

runtime_row.subject: Maths
runtime_row.questionText: A local Outdoors Club has just hiked to the south rim of a large canyon, when they spot a climber attempting to scale the taller northern face. The distance between the sheer walls of the northern and southern faces of the canyon is approximately 175 m. They sight an angle of depression of 60° to the bottom of the north face, and angles of elevation of 30° and 45° to the climber and to the top of the northern rim respectively. (a) How high is the southern rim of the canyon? (b) How high is the northern rim? (c) How much farther until the climber reaches the top?
solutionSteps: [1 mark] The observers at the south rim look across the canyon (horizontal distance 175 m). Angle of depression 60° to the bottom of the north face gives the height of the south rim above the canyon floor = 175 × tan60° = 175√3 ≈ 303.1 m.
[1 mark] Angle of elevation 45° to the top of the north rim gives height above eye-level = 175 × tan45° = 175 m. So height of north rim above the canyon floor = 303.1 + 175 = 478.1 m.

[1 mark] Angle of elevation 30° to the climber gives the climber's height above eye-level = 175 × tan30° = 175/√3 ≈ 101.0 m. Distance the climber still has to climb = (height above eye-level of top) − (of climber) = 175 − 101.0 ≈ 74 m.
runtime_row.finalAnswer: (a) Southern rim ≈ 303.1 m; (b) Northern rim ≈ 478.1 m; (c) ≈ 74 m remaining
runtime_row.diagramDescription: Cross-section of a canyon: a vertical south wall (left) where the observers stand at the top, and a taller vertical north wall (right). Horizontal gap between the walls = 175 m, drawn at the observers' eye level. From the observer's horizontal line of sight: a line angled 60° downward to the foot of the north wall, a line 30° upward to the climber on the north wall, and a line 45° upward to the top of the north rim.

runtime_row.questionText: From her elevated observation post 300 m (horizontally) away, a naturalist spots a troop of baboons high up in a tree. The angle of depression to the bottom of the tree is 30°, the angle of elevation to the top of the tree is 60°, and the angle of elevation to the troop of baboons is 45°. Find (a) the height of the observation post, (b) the height of the baboons' tree, and (c) the height of the baboons above ground.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] (a) Height of post = horizontal distance × tan(angle of depression to tree base) = 300 × tan 30° = 300/√3 = 100√3 ≈ 173.2 m.
[1 mark] (b) Height of tree top above the post level = 300 × tan 60° = 300√3 m. Height of tree = (top above post) + (post height above tree base) = 300√3 + 100√3 = 400√3 ≈ 692.8 m.
[1 mark] (c) Height of baboons above the post level = 300 × tan 45° = 300 m. Height of baboons above the ground = post height + 300 = 100√3 + 300 ≈ 473.2 m.

From the post's sight line: a downward 30° line to the tree base (ground), an upward 45° line to the baboons on the trunk, and an upward 60° line to the tree top. The tree is vertical on the right.

runtime_row.questionText: From the top of a 20 m high building, the angle of depression of a car on the road is 30 deg. Find the distance of the car from the foot of the building and the line of sight.
runtime_row.answer: Distance = 20sqrt(3) m and line of sight = 40 m.
runtime_row.explanation: Let the distance of the car from the foot of the building be x m. Angle of elevation from the car is 30 deg, so tan 30 deg = 20/x. This gives x = 20sqrt(3) m. Using sin 30 deg = 20/line of sight, the line of sight is 40 m. Final answer: Distance = 20sqrt(3) m and line of sight = 40 m.

runtime_row.questionText: From a point on the ground 15 m from the foot of a tower, the angle of elevation of the top is 60 deg. Find the height of the tower and the line joining the point to the top.
runtime_row.answer: Height = 15sqrt(3) m and line joining point to top = 30 m.
runtime_row.explanation: Let the height of the tower be h m. Using tan 60 deg = h/15, we get h = 15sqrt(3) m. Now use cos 60 deg = 15/line joining point to top. So the required slant line is 30 m. Final answer: Height = 15sqrt(3) m and line joining point to top = 30 m.
